sector_selloff.description: Three chip names fall together -- one story, not three.
sector_selloff.first_output:
The semiconductor names you're tracking took a sharp hit today -- NVDA down 6.1%, AMD off 5.4%, and MU leading the losses at 7.2% -- alongside headlines about widening chip export rules. All three moved together, with the sector index posting its worst session since March. KO was flat at +0.2%.

This was a tech-heavy selloff, with the Nasdaq 100 down 1.2% versus 0.4% for the broader S&P 500. The headlines point to tightening memory rules specifically, which may be related to MU's steeper decline, though all three chip names saw substantial volume.

Nothing notable beyond your watchlist today. The next earnings on your list is AMD in 30 days on November 7th, with KO, MU, and NVDA all reporting the same day.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.2%, more than twice the S&P 500's 0.4% decline, reflecting the weight semiconductors carry in that index.

All four names on your watchlist report in 30 days.
